name: Barbell Cossack Squat
description: A barbell-loaded version of the cossack squat, a lateral squat pattern that trains unilateral quad and hip strength through a large range of lateral motion. The loaded version increases mechanical demand on the working leg's quad, adductor, and glute while also training hip mobility under load.

execution.starting_position: Position a barbell on your upper back as for a back squat. Stand with feet significantly wider than shoulder width.
execution.setup_instructions: Set up the barbell in a rack to the correct height for a back squat. Unrack and walk out to a wide stance.
steps: Step 1: Shift your weight to one side, bending that knee deeply while keeping the opposite leg straight.
Step 2: Lower yourself into a full lateral squat on the working side, keeping the working foot fully flat.
Step 3: The straight leg remains extended on the floor with the toes pointing up or slightly outward.
Step 4: Drive through the working leg heel to return to the center and repeat on the opposite side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent. Exhale on the drive to center.
common_mistakes: Allowing the working heel to lift off the floor
safety_considerations: Ensure adequate hip mobility before loading — practice the bodyweight version first
Keep the bar securely on the upper back
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Deep lateral squat with the working thigh well below parallel. Opposite leg extended.
coaching_cues: Foot stays flat on the working side
Sit into the hip of the working leg
